gap: No result ChatGPT got states how big a picture each mini projector can light to the SMPTE dark-room target of 16 fL on battery for a full movie. Using measured battery-mode lumens, that is about 56 in for the XGIMI MoGo 4 (ECO), 55 in for the Nebula Mars 3 Air (Eco) and 49 in for the Nebula Capsule 3. None of them gets near the 100–120 in that the makers advertise.
standout_why: Three rival pages would not load past their intros. The RTINGS portable list and the TechRadar portable list returned only navigation and the intro, with no picks or numbers. The Wirecutter proxy URL ChatGPT cited returns a block message, and nytimes.com cannot be fetched. So I could not confirm what those pages say. The measured lumens behind this figure come from ProjectorCentral and The Hook Up, and neither appears in ChatGPT's results. ChatGPT's own answer quotes only rated lumens (450 ISO, 400 ANSI, 200 ANSI, 550 ISO) and gives no battery-mode brightness or screen size. Score is 2, not 3, because I could not check the rival pages' contents.
decides: This confirms the MoGo 4 as the pick at $479 but changes how it is sold. On battery for a whole film, ProjectorCentral's numbers say to plan for about a 56 in image, not 120 in. The MoGo 4's 258 lm Standard mode (about 74 in) lasted only a 90-minute film in ProjectorCentral's test. The Mars 3 Air lights about the same size in Eco (55 in) and lasted longest on battery: 3 h 10 min in ProjectorCentral's test. So it is the better pick when a 2.5-hour movie must finish on battery. The Capsule 3 is the smallest unit but only fills about 49 in on battery, so it should be described as a bedroom or ceiling projector for small images. Plugged in, the MoGo 4 (Performance) and Mars 3 Air (Standard) both reach about 90 in at 16 fL.

findings.label: Formula: 16:9 diagonal at a target brightness
findings.note: Arithmetic only, and the source URL is just the review the lumens come from. It assumes a matte white 1.0-gain screen. Area in ft² = lumens ÷ fL, and a 16:9 image's area = 0.4273 × diagonal² in². 16 fL is the usual SMPTE dark-room cinema target. I did not open a page stating that standard, so cite it as a convention, not a sourced figure.
